fr:title.text: claudemacs: an Emacs-native Claude Code frontend (progress)

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: claudemacs: an Emacs-native Claude Code frontend (progress)

fr:mainmatter.html:p: What it is. claude-comint (working name claudemacs) is an Emacs-native, multi-session frontend for the Claude Code CLI. It drives claude in stream-json mode (--input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json) and renders the conversation into Emacs buffers, so the agent and I live in the same Emacs session. It currently lives in my nix-config at ~/nix-config/emacs/.emacs.d/claude/claude-comint.el.

Design goal. At least the functionality of the Claude Code TUI, but better where Emacs helps: a comint-style input/output split, richer diffs and previews dispatched into real buffers, the agent reaching into the live Emacs session (running elisp, reading and editing buffers), and the agent editing the same session I am working in.

Built so far. Multiple concurrent sessions with an agent-view dashboard (dired-style mark/execute deletion); resume and persistent rename, both with column-aligned pickers; per-session working directory; visible streaming with a runtime timer and a live context-token gauge in the header; inline syntax-highlighted diffs and tool-result blocks that expand to the actual file on RET; a live plan buffer from TodoWrite; message queueing and mid-turn steering; and background shell jobs that report their output back when they finish.

Permissions are one live knob. A PreToolUse hook bridges each tool call to Emacs via emacsclient and prompts in a non-blocking buffer — you decide when you choose to, with no keystroke capture from other buffers. The hook is always registered; whether it actually prompts is read live, so toggling needs no process restart. The CLI --permission-mode is pinned to bypassPermissions underneath so the hook is the sole gate.

Non-blocking approvals throughout. The emacs-shell / eval / edit / read channels and the permission prompt all use the same non-blocking decision buffer instead of a blocking read-char, via a continuation-passing approval loop — so a prompt never steals input meant for another buffer.

Next steps. Hoist the package out of nix-config into its own directory and repo (claudemacs). Fix the input window auto-grow: it scrolls down a line as it grows, and should be capped at half the frame height. A code-cleanup and audit pass over the whole file. An in-input cbonsai screensaver (an overlay that yields to typing so steering still works) remains an optional nicety.
Related: My Forester Emacs mode setup.

My editing environment for .tree files is a two-layer stack: the upstream forester.el major mode plus my own large forester-org.el extension. Both live in one repo at ~/forester.el, which is my fork of ToposInstitute/forester.el (origin = stschaef/forester.el, with upstream pointing at Topos).

forester.el (upstream, Topos Institute) — the base major mode: syntax/font-lock for forester markup, rainbow-delimiters, and a handful of wrapper commands. This is the file autoloaded for .tree buffers. I carry a few personal patches on top of upstream (hard-coded forest root, rg-based grep, forester-find-title).

forester-org.el (mine, ~168 KB, ~190 interactive commands) — an org-mode-style workflow layer built entirely on tags in .tree files, with no compiler modifications. It provides tree navigation/creation (find, capture, daily notes), TODO state management, an agenda buffer, a cached query engine (forester query all plus filter combinators) with result buffers, Apple Reminders/Calendar sync via osascript, eglot LSP integration, in-Emacs HTML preview via shr, and the SPC r keybinding suite via general.el. It was originally developed inside ~/ocaml-forester, then imported into the forester.el repo (commit c0f244c); it no longer lives in ocaml-forester.

How it loads. ~/.emacs.d/packages.el adds ~/forester.el to load-path, autoloads forester-mode for .tree files, and registers autoload stubs for the forester-org commands so keybinds.el can bind them by symbol (the commandp check passes before bodies exist). ~/.emacs.d/init.el then does (require 'forester-org) eagerly, after all config files run, to fill in the real command bodies before any keybinding fires.
Keybindings. The SPC r ... prefix and the Evil keymaps for forester-org-agenda-mode, forester-query-mode, and forester-preview-mode are defined in ~/.emacs.d/keybinds.el.
Not in use. ~/forester_emacs_mode (GitHub stschaef/forester-emacs-mode) is an early-2025 standalone forester.el that has been superseded by the ~/forester.el fork. It can be ignored.
